first.rationale: Three pressures compete for the single experiment slot: competitor pricing erosion, activation decline, and onboarding completion decline. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the most tempting reaction to the competitor threat, but its consolidated claim of 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' predates the current competitive dynamic and doesn't address whether the acquired revenue is durable/qualified — a direct risk to the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I want the original record verified before ever committing budget to it. Onboarding completion and activation are both degrading right now, are mechanically linked (incomplete onboarding suppresses first-week activation), and have strong, more recent, self-serve-segment evidence (memory_86, memory_31) supporting a low-risk, reversible intervention. Fixing this funnel leak also indirectly protects conversion of any price-sensitive traffic the competitor threat exposes, without locking in margin-eroding pricing moves before their revenue-quality tradeoffs are re-examined. I'm verifying memory_86 (onboarding) to confirm the effect generalizes to the current regression rather than being a one-time artifact, and memory_73 (pricing) because it's the highest-stakes alternative I'm consciously deferring. Running this as a standard experiment rather than broad rollout preserves the option to revisit pricing or referral incentives next cycle once verified.
